title: Isaiah and David: God blots out iniquities; Acts calls to repentance
source_text: III. Sic vero Deus ipse apud Isaiam populum suum solatur, Ego sum, ego sum ipse qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter me, & peccatorum tuorum non recordabor, Isa. 43. Item, Delevi ut nubem iniquitates tuas, & quasi nebulam peccata tua. Isa. 44. Unde est quod fideles a Deo fidenter hanc gratiam implorant, quemadmodum David, Psal. 51. Avertere, inquit, faciem tuam a peccatis meis, & omnes iniquitates meas dele. Et ejusdem gratiae spe peccatores ad poenitentiam & conversionem invitantur. Poenitemini & convertimini, inquit Petrus Apostolus, ut deleantur peccata vestra, Act. 3.
pass_a_gloss: So also God himself consoles his people in Isaiah: I am, I myself am he who blots out your iniquities for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins (Isaiah 43). Likewise, I have blotted out your iniquities as a cloud, and your sins as a mist (Isaiah 44). Hence the faithful confidently beg this grace from God, as David does (Psalm 51): Turn away your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities. And by hope of the same grace sinners are invited to repentance and conversion. Repent and be converted, says the Apostle Peter, that your sins may be blotted out (Acts 3).
pass_b_english: Isaiah 43-44: God blots out iniquities and will not remember sins.
David (Psalm 51) and Peter (Acts 3) seek and invite that blotting-out.
